McDonald's will let customers build their own burgers for the first time | McDonald's

Hold the pickles, onions and special sauce. The Big Mac is becoming a victim of finicky tastes.

McDonald’s is planning major changes in the US as sales continue to slide. The burger chain’s plans to stop the decline include an expansion of a test that lets people build their own burgers by tapping on a touchscreen.


The company said Monday that it plans to expand the option to 2,000 of its 14,000 US locations by next year. The move could be part of McDonald’s plan to improve “technology,” an intention that caused many to speculate that workers would be replaced with robots.


The “Create Your Taste” program is a major departure for McDonald’s, which is built to deliver menu items like Quarter Pounders consistently, quickly and affordably. That model has come under pressure with the popularity of places like Chipotle, which stresses higher-quality ingredients and let people dictate exactly which toppings they want on their burritos and bowls.

Industry executives and analysts have noted the growing demand for customized orders, particularly among people in their 20s and 30s. They also note people are showing greater concern for the ingredients in their food.

McDonald’s has been struggling with declining sales in the US and said on Monday the figure fell 4.6% in November at established locations. The figure also fell 4% in the unit that includes the Asia-Pacific region, where the company is fighting to recover from a food-safety scandal. Overall, global sales declined 2.2% for the month.

Back in the US, CEO Don Thompson has conceded the company hasn’t done enough to keep up with shifting habits and said in October that changes are in store for its US restaurants.

Offering greater personalization could be a challenge for McDonald’s, however. The customized burgers take longer to prepare and are more expensive, and it’s not clear whether people will be willing to wait longer or shell out more money for a burger from McDonald’s. The locations that have the “Create Your Taste” option still have its regular menu as well.

McDonald’s has already announced the customized burgers will be expanded nationally in Australia.

McDonald’s is facing a number of others challenges, too, including perceptions of the freshness and quality of its ingredients. The chain has been trying to address such concerns with a new campaign that answers questions about its food, such as, “Does McDonald’s beef contain worms?”

In Asia, McDonald’s has been trying to bounce back since the summer, when a TV report in China showed workers at one of its suppliers repackaging meat that was alleged to be expired. The claim has not been publicly confirmed by the supplier or the government.

The Oak Brook, Illinois, company said comparable sales for Europe fell 2% with a strong performance in the UK more than offset by weakness in Russia, France and Germany.

McDonald’s has more than 35,000 locations in more than 100 countries. Its stock fell $2.81, or 2.9%, to $93.50 before the market opened Monday.

webpage.text:
“Momma, I wanna eat at the McDonald’s tonight”

The everyday sales conundrum

Recently I was at a job interview where the recruiter caught me off guard with a question which I never expected.

“Please differentiate sales and marketing.”

After spending more than 11 years in a well-traveled sales job, I least expected such a fundamental question at the job interview. I thought the recruiter would ask my take on social media marketing, inbound marketing, salesforce, hubspot, business analytics, etc. Well, I took some extra seconds to organize my thoughts before answering the question :-)

We know sales is the exchange of values for the mutual benefit of the parties involved. Marketing facilitate this exchange by defining the values to be exchanged. Well, that could be the simplest and crude definition we may put forward. As we all know, the traditional label of a talkative salesman is no more. In this digital age, sales is SAy LESs and listen more! The strong signals are audible to everybody in the market. A smart salesman picks up the weak signals from the market place and plays the game to perfection. If you are only doing the talking in sales, you will miss out the weak signals. If you open up your mind and hone your listening skills, you will start hearing the inner voices of the customers. To me, sales is an everyday affair or rather a way of life. Everybody is selling something every moment, only the values exchanged may change.

It was raining heavily and after my interview, I headed to the Mc Donald’s to ease my hunger pangs. As I settled at a corner table with my favorite spicy chicken wrap, a small family caught my attention. Father in business suit, mother with a handful of shopping bags and son with a winning smile on his face ordering at the counter. My intriguing salesman mind wanted to imagine the situation that led the family to Mc Donald’s on a rainy evening.

**************************************************************************

Mom Jennifer had her shower after work and got ready to catch up her favourite soap opera on the TV. It was raining heavily outside and a perfect evening to crawl up on the sofa. Little son Tommy jolted out from his room and shouted at his mother.

“Momma, I wanna eat at the Mc Donald’s tonight!”

Surely not pleased, mom gave him a mean look.

“It is raining heavily! I am going to prepare soup for dinner. Go and do your homework, now!”

Little Tommy retracted to his room only to appear again after five minutes with some flyer in his hands.

“Momma, do you want these discount coupons? Or shall I throw it away?”

Jennifer rolled her eyes hearing the word ‘discount’.

“What discount coupons? Where you got it from?”

“Aunt Jessica gave me on my way back to home. She was carrying a lot of shopping bags!”

“Aunt Jessica! Give that to me!” Jennifer switched off the TV.

“Momma, look! Up to 50% discount on hand bags and yeah the sale is ending today!”

By this time, Jennifer snatched away the flyer from Tommy.

Tommy remembered momma’s complaint to dad a week ago regarding the old torn handbag. Dad promised a new handbag as birth day gift which is three months away.

Tommy continued, “ Anyway, you wanted a new hand bag. Ask dad to come to the shopping mall after work so that you can shop together. By the way, the Mc Donald’s is next to the shop and open 24 hours. I can wait there completing my homework while you do the shopping.”

You know what happened next? Little Tommy finally ate at the Mc Donald’s that evening.

What a great value proposition! Little Tommy proved to be an amazing salesman. Let us look at the different sales and marketing principles applied in this simple household situation.

Product: The proposal to eat at the Mc Donald’s

Customer: Momma Jennifer

Salesman: Little Tommy

The market environment was not in the favor of the salesman. It was raining heavily outside and the customer did not want to face the harsh environment by venturing outside. She was happy and keen to catch up on her favorite TV show. No external disturbance was expected or tolerated. Eating outside was the last thing in her mind. She would rather order online and eat at home. But the salesman wants to be at the Mc Donald’s that evening for the experience of eating out.

His first attempt to sell the product failed. The customer cited the harsh environmental conditions (could be a bad economy in a commercial sales situation) and reminded the salesman to go and do his homework:-) A clear signal that the salesman was approaching a wrong customer. He did not give up by hearing the "No!" from the customer. He clearly understood that sales is a rejection business. He retracted and changed his sales strategy. He already did his market research and got all the information at hand. He cleverly uncovered a hidden need of the customer – the need for a new hand bag. He overheard the conversation between his parents last week. He picked up the weak signals from the market and used it to form his sales strategy.

He also got other resources at hand. He knew the customer’s competition. Aunt Rebecca is the competition. When the customer heard that the competition is taking advantage of a favorable market condition (discounted sale), she wanted to know more. The salesman whipped out the flyer and shared the market information with the customer. He also added a time-pressure to the situation – the sale is ending today! A sense of urgency was created and the customer needed to act fast to keep abreast of the competition.

The salesman also helped the customer by organizing the financial resources and making the shopping a family bonding time (experiential marketing). He suggested to get dad at the shopping mall. We all know, dad funded the shopping and dinner. Dad also carried the shopping bags!

The salesman added more value to the proposition. He made the customer feel that shopping is the first priority (meeting the hidden need of the customer) and eating at Mc Donald’s is a by-product of the whole experience. He put customer first! He also volunteered to stay at the Mc Donald’s doing his homework. What a good boy! He gave the customer her space to shop freely without any disturbance or pressure from the salesman.

The 4 P’s of marketing are aptly applied. The salesman knew the right people to approach, the place, the promotion and the price! The salesman got rewarded at the Mc Donald’s with his favourite meal combo. He did some upselling by asking for a cone ice cream on his way out of the Mc Donald’s.

That night, he might have hugged his mom and planted a sincere kiss on her cheek. “Good night momma, thank you for the treat.”

Vow, that was customer appreciation!

An elated mom winked at him and whispered into his ears “Next time you get shopping coupons, you must give it to me:-)."

Boy, that was inbound marketing!!

McDonald's serves up rising UK sales despite troubles in the US | McDonald's

McDonald’s might be slipping up in the US, its home market, but in the UK the fast food chain enjoyed another year of growth, according to figures for 2014.

Turnover for the group’s UK operation increased by £67.5m to £1.4bn, even though the group is increasingly franchising restaurants, which tends to reduce revenues.

McDonald’s said the improving economic outlook in the UK in 2014 resulted in increased sales and margins but added that its high street estate continued to be impacted by declining retail footfall.

The fast food restaurant operator has tried to counter the reduced traffic on the high street by upgrading its voucher scheme for customers who visit affected restaurants.

Profit before tax for 2014 came in at £225m, compared with £244.9m, on which the UK operation paid tax of £57.7m, up from £49.95m the previous year.

A McDonald’s spokesperson said: “We are testing some new concepts, such as table service, whereby customers place their order via our new digital kiosks and then have their food brought to them. To date this has been well received and we will continue to review and rollout when appropriate over the coming months.”

On wage costs and the implementation of a “national living wage”, McDonald’s said it was working through the implications to see how it would impact the business.The corporation has generally enjoyed a consistent performance in the UK, even when it has been in decline in the US. The group is currently run by a Briton, Steve Easterbrook, who has been trying to revive the chain, which is facing fierce competition from rivals such as Five Guys and Shake Shack.

Britain’s first McDonald’s opened in 1974 and there are now more than 1,250 in the UK.

webpage.text:
麥當勞的 “I’m lovin’ it” 是什麼意思？文法上正確嗎？

在文法上其實像 like, love, hate, want, need 等字都是不能用進行式的
但大家可能會覺得奇怪：麥當勞是個美國公司，怎麼會把 I’m lovin’ it 這句文法好像不對的話印在產品上呢？
事實上在這句話裡，love 的意思不是平常的「愛」
否則翻譯成「我正在愛它」的確很奇怪
這裡的 love 其實是 enjoy「享受，享用」的意思
表示吃的人正吃得很開心
而為什麼要寫成 lovin’ 而不是 loving 呢？
這是一種用拚字來表現說話口音的方式
因為在講話快的時候，美式口音常會把字尾的 ing [ ɪŋ ] 唸得像 [ ən ]
用一撇取代 g 表示有個字母被省掉了
這種寫法常在歌詞裡或對話台詞中看到
模擬大家在日常生活中真正講話的方式，會比較貼近大眾，產生親切感
就像我們現在的中文流行語會看到用「醬子」來取代「這樣子」的俏皮寫法
